title: Provision Lambda Invoke Permission
scenario: Your platform team needs Lambda Invoke Permission for allowing API Gateway to invoke a function. Write a reusable Terraform configuration that provisions it, drives every input through variables, applies the standard tags, and exports the operational identifiers.
constraints: Create exactly one resource of type aws_lambda_permission.
All configurable values must come from variables declared in variables.tf.
Code must pass terraform fmt conventions (2-space indents, trailing newline, no tabs).

focus.title: Complete the aws_lambda_permission resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_lambda_permission.

hints.why: Lambda packages compute as a small, event-driven unit. The code artifact, execution role and trigger are the contract to get right.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_lambda_permission" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_lambda_permission. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use Lambda for short-lived event handlers or glue code where managing a server would add cost and operational noise.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_lambda_permission" "this"`. Use this code shape: statement_id; action; function_name; principal. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.lambda_function_name`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
